directAnswer: Pope John XVII reigned for less than six months in 1003, from May to November. Born John Sicco, he was chosen under the influence of the Roman patrician John Crescentius, and he is unusual in having been married with sons before entering the clergy.

paras: After Sylvester II's death in May 1003, power in Rome lay with John Crescentius, son of the Crescentius II executed in 1998. The new pope, John Sicco, was elected with his support. With no strong emperor present in Italy, the papacy once again depended on the Roman nobility.

sections.h2: A Pope Who Had Been Married
paras: The sources record that John Sicco had been married before his ordination and had three sons, all of whom became priests. In the early medieval Church, it was not unusual for a married man to be ordained after his wife's death or with her consent to separate, and this does not imply scandal.

John XVII died on 6 November 1003, after a pontificate of about six months. Few documents survive from his reign, and the Liber Pontificalis gives only basic information. He was buried in St. John Lateran.

keyFacts: Elected under the influence of the patrician John Crescentius
Married with three sons, all priests, before ordination

faqs.question: Was Pope John XVII married?
faqs.answer: Yes, before entering the clergy. He had three sons, all of whom became priests.

faqs.question: Who controlled Rome during John XVII's reign?
faqs.answer: John Crescentius, a member of the powerful Crescentii family, held the dominant position in the city.
